label: Collection, aggregation, correlation, archiving and reporting

mentor.diagnosis: You treated the SIEM as one undifferentiated thing. The pipeline has stages, and questions usually point at exactly one of them.
contrast: Agents or forwarders gather events from sources
A source nobody onboarded, so the evidence never existed
Events from many sources are normalised into one searchable store
Different time zones and formats, so nothing lines up
Rules combine events across sources into a single meaningful alert
Thousands of raw events and no alert anyone acts on
Older data moved to cheaper storage for retention and legal need
Retention shorter than the time it takes to detect a breach
Summaries and trends for operations and for compliance
Reports nobody reads, mistaken for monitoring
mentor.rule: Aggregation puts everything in one place; correlation is what turns many events into one alert. A question about seeing a pattern across firewall, endpoint and directory logs is a correlation question.
mentor.tell: Several sources that must be combined, or a retention period that ended before anyone looked.
mentor.trap: Archiving is treated as housekeeping. If the mean time to detect a breach exceeds your retention window, the evidence is gone before the investigation starts.
